sceneHappening: Press on to maturity; a solemn warning; the anchor of hope in God's oath
summary: "Therefore leaving the teaching of the first principles of Christ, let's press on to perfection—not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, of faith toward God, of the teaching of baptisms, of laying on of hands, of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment. This will we do, if God permits." Then the warning: "For concerning those who were once enlightened and tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit, and tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come, and then fell away, it is impossible to renew them again to repentance; seeing they crucify the Son of God for themselves again, and put him to open shame." The picture of land follows: land that drinks the rain and produces a crop "receives blessing from God; but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is rejected and near being cursed, whose end is to be burned." "But, beloved, we are persuaded of better things for you, and things that accompany salvation, even though we speak like this. For God is not unrighteous, so as to forget your work and the labor of love which you showed toward his name, in that you served the saints, and still do serve them." The readers are to show diligence "to the fullness of hope even to the end," imitating those who inherited the promises. God swore to Abraham by himself, "that by two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to take hold of the hope set before us. This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast and entering into that which is within the veil; where as a forerunner Jesus entered for us, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek."
whySettingMatters: Verses 4-8 are among the most debated in the New Testament. The people described have been enlightened, have tasted the heavenly gift, shared in the Holy Spirit, and tasted God's word, and then "fell away." Readers have taken these words in several ways: as describing true believers who can lose salvation; as describing people who came close without true faith (compare Matthew 7:21-23 and the parable of the soils in Matthew 13); as a real warning that is not meant to describe what will happen to these readers, so that the warning itself is God's means of keeping them (the author says in 6:9 that he is persuaded of "better things"); or as a hypothetical case stated to show how serious abandoning Christ would be. The reason given is that to leave Christ is to "crucify the Son of God again": there is no second sacrifice (10:26). The phrase "impossible to renew them" has also been read as a statement about human ability, not God's. In reading it, readers should notice that the passage is addressed to a community drifting toward leaving, and the writer's next words are of confidence and encouragement. The two "immutable things" in 6:18 are God's promise and his oath (Genesis 22:16-17). The anchor of hope "entering into that which is within the veil" (6:19) draws on the temple: Jesus has gone ahead as a "forerunner" into God's presence, and hope clings to where he is. An anchor is a rare image for hope in ancient writing, though anchors appear on early Christian tombs.

people.note: Urges the readers on, warns them, and then voices confidence.
Told to press on to maturity and to hold to the hope.
To whom God swore by himself and who obtained the promise by patient endurance.
The forerunner who entered within the veil as a high priest forever.

questions: "Let's press on to perfection" (maturity). What do you think it would mean for your own community to move on from the basics?
The warning in 6:4-6 has troubled many readers. How do verse 9 and the rest of the chapter help you read it?
The image of the land that drinks rain and bears either crops or thorns points to what we do with what we receive. What fruit does the letter look for?
"An anchor of the soul... within the veil." What does it mean for hope to be fastened to where Jesus already is?
